shorts.title: A Crocodile's Face Is More Sensitive Than Your Fingertip
shorts.hook: A crocodile's face can feel more than your fingertip.
shorts.outro: So Doug sat perfectly still in a canoe, in the dark, in the middle of the river. One drop fell. Full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHAT HAPPENED WHEN DOUG'S DROP FELL?
shorts.description: The tiny dots on a crocodile's jaw are touch sensors that can feel forces ten times smaller than your fingertip can, and the full episode shows what one drop of water did to Doug sitting still in a canoe at night.

shorts.title: This Crocodile Swam 411 Kilometers Home in 20 Days
shorts.hook: Scientists moved a crocodile across Cape York. It swam home anyway.
shorts.outro: Doug drove one a very long way from home and waited three months. Then he went to run a bath. Full video below.
shorts.description: Scientists flew a satellite-tagged saltwater crocodile across Cape York and it swam all the way around the tip to get home, and the full episode reveals what turned up in Doug's bathtub after he tried the same trick.

shorts.title: Cassius the Crocodile Was Thought to Be Over 110 Years Old
shorts.hook: This crocodile may have hatched before the First World War.
shorts.outro: Doug brought a tape measure, ran out of tape at the back legs, and patted it on the nose. Full video below.
shorts.description: Cassius, a five and a half meter saltwater crocodile in Queensland, may have hatched around the start of the First World War, and the full episode reveals whether the sleeping giant woke up when Doug patted its nose.

shorts.title: This Saltwater Crocodile Stayed Underwater for 11.5 Hours
shorts.hook: One crocodile stayed underwater for eleven and a half hours.
shorts.outro: Doug watched that river for an hour, called it empty, and waded in with a fishing rod. Full video below.
shorts.description: A resting crocodile can stay underwater for at least eight hours and one was recorded on a dive of eleven and a half, and the full episode reveals whether the river Doug called empty really was.
